chunks: A section of the People of the Book say: 'Believe in the morning what has been revealed to the faithful, and deny in the evening; they might perhaps turn back.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)
key_terms.وَجْهَ النَّهَارِ: The face of the day / morning

ai.seo_question: What was the hypocritical strategy of the People of the Book mentioned in Surah Al Imran?
ai.summary: This verse highlights the phenomenon of *Taqiyya* (dissimulation) practiced by a faction of the People of the Book, specifically the Jews of Medina, who adopted a dual identity to maintain political leverage and avoid persecution. Shia scholars note that while their intent was deceptive, it serves as a parallel to the Shia practice of concealing faith under pressure, though theirs was often for strategic survival rather than religious preservation. The verse underscores the complexity of early Islamic community dynamics, where public conformity did not always reflect inner conviction.
